channel.title: AI News Digest
channel.description: Official AI product updates from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and GitHub

item.title: The Lenfest Institute grows landmark program with expanded OpenAI support
item.description: OpenAI is expanding the Lenfest AI Collaborative and Fellowship Program with $5 million in funding and up to $5 million in software credits and engineering support.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Anthropic’s newest Sonnet model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for well-scoped everyday work like building features and fixing bugs.

item.title: thinking: {"type": "between_tools"}
item.description: Code written for Claude Sonnet 5 can break on Claude Sonnet 5.5 in five ways. To turn off up-front thinking, send thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} instead of "disabled", at high effort or below. Forced tool use ( tool_choice types any and tool ) returns a 400 error. Thinking blocks are tied to the model and the conversation. On the Claude API and Google Cloud, the earlier computer_20251124 computer use tool isn't accepted.

item.title: Preserved thinking
item.description: Thinking blocks that Claude Sonnet 5.5 produces work only in the account that produced them, or in an account linked to it. When another account sends one of these blocks, the API drops the block before the model sees it, and the request succeeds. Blocks from earlier models aren't affected. See Preserved thinking.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
item.description: We've launched Claude Sonnet 5.5 ( claude-sonnet-5-5 ). It's available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry. For its context window, output limits, and prices, see the Claude Sonnet 5.5 model page.

item.title: Proaction boosts sales 60% and saves 75+ hours with Codex
item.description: With Codex, GPT-Live-1, and GPT-6 Astra, Proaction builds, operates, and sells modern fleet management faster.

item.title: Semantic governance policies support VPC Service Controls (Preview)
item.description: Feature Semantic governance policies support VPC Service Controls (Preview) Semantic governance policy and the Semantic governance policy engine support VPC Service Controls in Preview. You can include Semantic governance policy and the policy engine in your service perimeter to help mitigate the risk of data exfiltration when governing agent tool calls. For more information, see VPC Service Controls with Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and Semantic governance policies overview.

item.title: Usage metrics API adds pull request review stages
item.description: The enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now break down how long pull requests spend in each stage of review. A new pull_request_review_times array on each repos-1-day row reports a median and a 90th percentile for the time from ready for review to first review, first review to final review, and final review to merge.

item.title: Updates to GitHub Copilot for Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description: GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams now gives you more context, more control, and a clearer path from conversation to GitHub work. Whether you’re sharing files in Slack or images and forwarded messages in Teams, Copilot can use more of the context already in your conversation.

item.title: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 21
item.description: This week’s releases add new models to Copilot, local sandboxing in the Copilot app, and updates to Copilot in Slack, Microsoft Teams, JetBrains, and VS Code. GitHub Copilot Claude Opus 5.5 is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans.

item.title: Enterprise managed settings in-product validator
item.description: You can now use an in-product validator for enterprise managed settings for GitHub Copilot. The validator detects malformed JSON, unsupported configurations, invalid team mappings, and other errors that can prevent policies from being enforced.

item.title: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory
item.description: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory for customers who’ve enabled it. When you use agentic autofix, it reviews existing memories for context that can help resolve security alerts.

item.title: Default Enablement of Copilot features for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description: We’re introducing a new global default policy for generally available GitHub Copilot features and supported client capabilities in enterprise and organization Copilot settings. For the next 28 days, you can configure this policy, but it won’t affect feature access for your users yet.

item.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
item.description: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar

item.title: Require proof of presence for high-impact actions
item.description: You can now require an interactive re-authentication or a multi-factor challenge before members take high-impact actions on GitHub Enterprise Cloud accounts. Proof of presence is an expansion of GitHub’s sudo mode for enterprises, enforcing a higher security bar when it’s needed.

item.title: stop_details.category
item.description: We're resuming billing for refusals that arrive before any output when stop_details.category is "bio", "frontier_llm", or "reasoning_extraction", the categories where we measure low volumes of false positives. Mid-stream refusals were already billed. Refusals billed under this change are charged like any other request, at the rates of the model that ran it. Refusals before any output in other categories are still not billed, and fallback credit is unchanged.

item.title: product_surface
item.description: The Compliance API local session endpoints are out of beta for Claude for Microsoft 365 sessions in Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook ( product_surface values beginning with office_agents ). See Sessions on users' machines.

item.title: Two years of OpenAI Academy
item.description: Marking two years of OpenAI Academy and bringing AI skills to even more communities.

item.title: Sam Altman’s remarks at the United Nations Security Council
item.description: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discusses AI safety, human control, and international cooperation in remarks to the United Nations Security Council.

item.title: Ringg’s AI agents resolve up to 65% of customer calls with OpenAI
item.description: Using GPT-5.6, Ringg powers multilingual agents across voice, chat, WhatsApp, and web for 90% less cost vs. GPT-4.1.

item.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
item.description: OpenAI is extending access to its Daybreak program to the Government of Ukraine to support the cyber defense of civilian infrastructure.

item.title: How invideo improves color grading 3x with GPT‑6 Astra
item.description: With GPT‑6 Astra, invideo plans edits with greater precision, improves color correction and grading threefold, and produces 50 custom effects in one day.

item.title: Introducing MentalHealthBench
item.description: MentalHealthBench is an expert-informed benchmark for evaluating helpful and safe AI responses across realistic mental health conversations.

item.title: Grab and OpenAI bring practical AI skills to Southeast Asia
item.description: OpenAI and Grab launch GO Forward with AI, a regional programme helping 30,000 partners build practical AI skills across Southeast Asia.

item.title: ChatGPT Ads expands to Southeast Asia and Taiwan
item.description: ChatGPT Ads is expanding to Southeast Asia and Taiwan, giving eligible businesses new ways to reach people across more than 60 countries.

item.title: Airbnb widens access to GPT-6 Astra and OpenAI frontier models
item.description: Learn how Airbnb is expanding access to GPT-6 Astra and OpenAI frontier models to help engineering teams solve bugs, design systems, and ship faster.

item.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
item.description: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello

item.title: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description: Local sandboxing helps reduce the potential impact of unintended commands by limiting access to files, network resources, and credentials on your machine. In the GitHub Copilot app, you configure it per project for local repository and working tree sessions.

item.title: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
item.description: GitHub Copilot code review now offers additional personal configurations to an expanded set of Copilot plans and an enterprise-level default setting. These improvements are now generally available: A dedicated personal settings page for automatic review and your default review effort An enterprise-wide default review effort setting for organization-owned repositories ⚙️ Manage your personal review settings Previously, personal Copilot code review settings were available only with Copilot Pro...

item.title: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description: Understand how Copilot agents perform and interact with models and tools. The GitHub Copilot app now supports OpenTelemetry (OTel) configuration through enterprise-managed settings.

item.title: New features and improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains 1.18.0 brings AI-assisted tool approvals, more control over agent conversations, and shared skills and instructions for your organization. You can also review plans with the Codex agent and manage MCP tools with persistent controls.

item.title: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system
item.description: In early results from our new life sciences research lab, Claude agents found an enzyme system whose function is still unknown.

item.title: cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07
item.description: Cache diagnostics is out of beta on the Claude API and no longer requires the cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07 beta header. Include the diagnostics object on a Messages request to opt in; requests that still send the header work as before. Responses from POST /v1/messages now always include the diagnostics field, which is null when the request did not include the diagnostics object.

item.title: Priorities and principles for effective third party assessments
item.description: OpenAI outlines priorities and principles for rigorous, secure, and independent third-party AI safety assessments of frontier models and safeguards.

item.title: Introducing GPT-6 Sol and Luna
item.description: Meet GPT-6 Sol and Luna, two models that bring frontier intelligence to everyday work with different balances of capability and cost.

item.title: Better prompt caching for GPT-6
item.description: Learn how GPT-6 improves prompt caching with higher cache hit rates, new diagnostics, explicit breakpoints, and controls that reduce latency and costs.

item.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna now available
item.description: OpenAI’s GPT-6 family is expanding in GitHub Copilot with two additional models: GPT-6 Sol, and GPT-6 Luna. Joining the previously released GPT-6 Astra, these new options let you select the model that best fits your task, whether that’s everyday agentic coding or fast, cost-efficient assistance.

item.title: Faster C++ code intelligence with whole codebase indexing
item.description: C++ code intelligence in GitHub Copilot CLI is now faster with support for whole codebase indexing. C++ repositories can contain millions of lines of code across deeply connected source files and headers.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic’s newest Opus model, is now available in GitHub Copilot. You can use it for agentic coding, long-running agentic tasks, and knowledge work.

item.title: inline-tools-2026-09-15
item.description: Tools can now be defined inside a mid-conversation system message, in beta on the Claude API with the inline-tools-2026-09-15 beta header. A tool_addition block can carry the tool's full definition ( tool: {"type": "tool_definition", "definition": {...}} ), so you can add a tool, change its schema, or move a server tool to a newer version without editing tools or invalidating the prompt cache. The same header covers adding and removing tools by reference.

item.title: Fast mode
item.description: Fast mode (research preview) is available for Claude Opus 5.5 on the Claude API.

item.title: thinking: {"type": "disabled"}
item.description: On Claude Opus 5.5, thinking can't be disabled: thinking: {"type": "disabled"} and thinking: {"type": "enabled",...} return a 400 error. Omit the thinking field and control thinking depth with the effort parameter. tool_choice types any and tool also return a 400 error, as on Claude Fable 5.1; use auto with strict tool use.

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5
item.description: We've launched Claude Opus 5.5 ( claude-opus-5-5 ), a model for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. It has a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking, at $4 / $20 USD per MTok (Claude Opus 5 is $5 / $25). Claude Opus 5.5 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry.

item.title: Expanding OpenAI Academy with new learning paths
item.description: Explore new OpenAI Academy learning paths for employees, developers, leaders, educators, and students to build and demonstrate practical AI skills.

item.title: Grok 4.7 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description: Grok 4.7, xAI’s latest reasoning model, is now rolling out in GitHub Copilot. Building on Grok 4.6, it is designed for agentic coding and complex, multistep workflows.

item.title: Introducing the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint
item.description: OpenAI introduces the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint, a six-pillar roadmap for safer AI experiences that protect and empower young people.

item.title: xAI's Grok 4.6 is generally available
item.description: Feature xAI's Grok 4.6 is generally available Grok 4.6 is now generally available (GA) and available for production use on the global endpoint and the US multi-region endpoint. Breaking Agent Platform SDK for Python version 2.0.1 is available Version 2.0.1 of the Agent Platform SDK for Python ( google-cloud-agentplatform ) is now available.
